# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.

# Repository Report: /app (transaction-enrichment-python)

## 1. Overall Structure

This is a Flask-based microservice ("categorizationapp") that receives Indian bank statement transactions as JSON, enriches each row with a `transactionCategory`, `transactionSubcategory` (e.g. SALARY), `partyName` (counterparty), `merchantType`, PFM categories, etc., and returns the enriched rows. All logic is regex/rule-driven over pandas DataFrames using `np.select(conditions, choices)` tables.

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                          # python:3.9.2, pip install -e ., gunicorn on port 9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # Flask, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, python-Levenshtein, scipy, scikit-learn
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app creation, request timing hooks
        ├── Controller.py               # HTTP endpoints; per-bank orchestration pipeline
        ├── BankScripts/                # 35 per-bank categorizer modules (HDFC.py, SBI.py, ICICI.py, Axis.py, Kotak.py, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/             # shared enrichment stages + regex constants
            ├── AppUtil.py              # df cleanup, sep_by_* splitters, py_extract, fuzzy_match
            ├── RegexConstants.py       # cross-bank regexes (SALARY, LOAN, TECHNICAL_BOUNCE, ...)
            ├── BankRegexConstants.py   # bank-specific regexes (HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN*, REVERSAL_*, FT_CHQ_PATTERN*, ...)
            ├── Purpose.py / CardPurpose.py          # subcategory ("purpose") assignment
            ├── CleanName.py / CardCleanNames.py     # partyName cleanup (1971 lines)
            ├── SalaryDetection.py      # clustering-based salary sub-tag
            ├── InternalPayment.py      # self-transfer detection via fuzzy name match
            ├── PFMCategorization.py, SimpleDescription.py, RecurrentTxns.py
            └── TransactionCategoryEnums.py, TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py
```

**Entry points** (`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`):
- `POST /categorizeTransaction` — `categorizeTransaction()` at line 69–70. Dispatches on `bank` to `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(...)`, then runs the shared pipeline: `card_clean_names`/`card_purpose` (credit cards) → `purpose()` → `clean_names()` → `internal_payment()` → `salary_detection()` (SAVING only) → `pfm_categorization()` + `simple_description()` (if `isPFMEnabled`). The per-bank blocks are near-identical copies (lines 91–~1000+).
- `POST /recurrentTransactions` — `recurrentTransactions()` line 55–56.
- Flask app: `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/__init__.py` line 7.

## 2. Labeling / Enrichment Logic Locations

**Category classification (per bank)** — each `BankScripts/<Bank>.py` has one `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` function containing ordered `[condition, choice]` regex rules with `np.select(..., default="TRANSFER")`. Representative example, `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py`:
- `categorize_HDFC_transactions()` line 9; first-level category table lines 11–104 (UPI, IMPS, NEFT, RTGS, ATM_WITHDRAWAL, CHARGES, etc.), default category is `TRANSFER` (line 104).
- Category/subcategory value enums: `TransactionCategoryEnums.py` (`TransactionCategory`, line 3) and `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` (`TransactionSubcategory`, line 3).

**Cheque deposit vs transfer detection** — inside each bank script; a credit row is `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` when narration/remark matches cheque patterns, otherwise falls through to default `TRANSFER`:
- HDFC.py lines 69–75 (CHQ/cheque narration rules, CREDIT→CHEQUE_DEPOSIT, DEBIT→CHEQUE_PAID), and the remark-based rule at line 100: 15-char remark matching `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` on CREDIT → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`.
- Similar remark-number heuristics: SBI.py 46–47, Axis.py 57–59, Kotak.py 64–65, PNB.py 58–61, YES.py 45/53, RBL.py 48–49, BankOfMaharashtra.py 65/74, etc.
- Cheque bounce chain: HDFC.py line 126 — a `CHEQUE_RETURN` immediately after `CHEQUE_PAID` with negative prior balance → subcategory `INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE`.
- Cheque narration regex constants: `BankRegexConstants.py` lines 80–90 (`HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1..10`), 139–148 (`PNB_CHQ_*`), 262–299 (`FT_CHQ_PATTERN1..37` — cheque-based fund-transfer parsing), 313–318 (`CHQ_PATTERN*`, `CHQ_CLEAN_KOTAK`).

**Salary sub-tag** —
- Rule-based: `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` — `purpose(transactions, accountType)` line 9; SALARY/SALARY_DISBURSED rules lines 14–17 using `SALARY`, `NOT_SAL`, `SAL_IMPS`, `SALARY_DISB` regexes from `RegexConstants.py`. Also per-bank shortcuts, e.g. HDFC.py lines 119, 124–125; SBI.py line 84.
- Statistical: `UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` — `salary_detection(transactions)` line 16. Clusters party names with Levenshtein distance + hierarchical clustering (`cut_tree(linkage(...))`, line 34), then tags recurring credits > 2999 as `SALARY` (Scenarios 1 and 2, lines 64–210), plus `REIMBURSEMENT` assignment (lines 124–140) and second-salary detection (lines 142–202). Called from Controller only for `accountType == "SAVING"`.

**Counterparty / payee name extraction from narration** —
- Per-bank `partyName` extraction tables, e.g. HDFC.py lines 146–221 (UPI/IMPS/NEFT dash-token slicing via `sep_by_dash`, POS patterns, cheque patterns lines 187–197, transfer patterns 199–215) with subsequent cleanup passes lines 225–273; `party2` (no-space variant) line 275.
- Global cleanup: `UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` — `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` line 9 (1971 lines of stop-word/company-name normalization). Credit-card variants in `CardCleanNames.py` (`card_clean_names`, line 9) and `CardPurpose.py` (`card_purpose`, line 9).
- Merchant/purpose enrichment on top of partyName: `Purpose.py` lines 180+ (`merchantType` such as NBFC/HFC), `PFMCategorization.py` (`pfm_categorization`, line 8), `SimpleDescription.py` (`simple_description`, line 6).

**Slash-delimited reference parsing** —
- `UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` — `sep_by_(description, n1, n2)` line 14–15 splits narration on `/` and joins tokens `[n1:n2]`; siblings `sep_by_dash`, `sep_by_wave`, `sep_by_star`, `sep_by_comma`, `sep_by_colon`, `sep_by_under`, bracket variants (lines 17–45); `py_extract()` (regex extract with NaN handling) lines 61–66; `fuzzy_match()` line 48.
- Usage examples: SBI.py line 99 (`UPI` → `sep_by_(description,3,4)`), lines 149–151 (IMPS token slicing); HDFC.py line 201 (single-slash TRANSFER/REVERSAL → `sep_by_(...,1,2)`); SouthIndian.py lines 64, 73 (last slash token for NACH/UPI).

**Reversal / bounce detection** —
- Per-bank rules, e.g. HDFC.py: UPI/IMPS/ATM/card reversals lines 21–25, `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` line 27, `NEFT_RETURN`/`RTGS_RETURN`/`CHEQUE_RETURN_PENALTY` lines 28–30, `CHEQUE_RETURN` lines 69–72, and pairwise debit-credit matching heuristics (same amount, adjacent rows) lines 98–99 → `REVERSAL`/`AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`.
- Bank-specific reversal regexes in `BankRegexConstants.py` (e.g. `REVERSAL_CANARA` 323, `REVERSAL_KV` 344, `REVERSAL_YES` 394, `AUTO_BOUNCE_KV` 343).
- Bounce-cause classification in `Purpose.py` lines 145–147 using `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` and `INSUFF_BOUNCE` regexes from `RegexConstants.py` lines 86–87 → subcategories `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` / `INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE`.
- Reversal/bounce categories are excluded downstream: SalaryDetection.py lines 45–46, InternalPayment.py line 16, PFMCategorization.py line 73 (maps all REVERSAL|REFUND|RETURN|BOUNCE to PFM "REVERSAL").

## 3. Tests

**There are no tests in this repository.** Findings:
- No `test*`/`*_test*` files, no `tests/` directory (repo contains only `Dockerfile`, `.gitignore`, `setup.py`, and the two source packages).
- No pytest/unittest/nose references anywhere; `setup.py` declares only runtime deps (Flask, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, scipy, scikit-learn, etc.), no `tests_require` or CI config (`.github/` absent).
- `.gitignore` mentions "Unit test reports TEST*.xml" but that is boilerplate; git history is a single commit ("import codebase").
- The only "testing" artifacts are commented-out dendrogram plotting blocks labeled "For testing purpose only" in `SalaryDetection.py` (lines 27–32) and `RecurrentTxns.py` (lines 16–21).

**How to run/exercise the app instead:** build via the Dockerfile (`pip3 install -e .` then `gunicorn -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app`), or run the Flask app directly, and POST JSON to `/categorizeTransaction` with `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, and a `transactions` array — this is effectively the only verification path available.

import sys, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
sys.path.insert(0, "/app/categorizationapp")

import pandas as pd
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.HDFC import categorize_HDFC_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.ICICI import categorize_ICICI_transactions
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.Purpose import purpose
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.CleanName import clean_names
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts import AppUtil

def run(bank, fn, rows, accountType="SAVING"):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df = AppUtil.clean_input_df(df)
    df = fn(df, accountType)
    df = purpose(df, accountType)
    df = clean_names(df, accountType, bank)
    return df

def row(desc, typ, amt, bal=10000.0, remark=""):
    return {"description": desc, "type": typ, "amount": amt,
            "balanceAfterTransaction": bal, "remark": remark}

print("=" * 100)
print("HDFC cases")
hdfc_rows = [
    # 1. mango_saver a: credit, remark = all-numeric 15-char (10 zeros + 5 digits) -> CHEQUE_DEPOSIT
    row("SOME DEPOSIT NOTE", "CREDIT", 25000.0, remark="000000000012345"),
    # 2. mango_saver b: salary credit, bare 6-digit numeric narration -> subcategory SALARY
    row("123456", "CREDIT", 55000.0),
    # 4. maintainer: matching debit then offsetting credit, same description w/ IMPS -> credit = REVERSAL
    row("IMPS-402913031234-JOHN DOE-HDFC-PAYMENT", "DEBIT", 5000.0),
    row("IMPS-402913031234-JOHN DOE-HDFC-PAYMENT", "CREDIT", 5000.0),
    # regression guards (should stay as-is)
    row("UPI-SWIGGY-SWIGGY@ICICI-ICIC0DC0099-101010101010-PAYMENT", "DEBIT", 250.0),
    row("NEFT CR-SBIN0000123-RAMESH KUMAR-ACME CORP-N123456789012345", "CREDIT", 12000.0),
    row("POS 416021XXXXXX1234 AMAZON INDIA", "DEBIT", 999.0),
    row("SALARY JAN 2021 ACME CORP", "CREDIT", 60000.0),
]
out = run("HDFC", categorize_HDFC_transactions, hdfc_rows)
print(out[["description", "remark", "type", "transactionCategory", "transactionSubcategory", "partyName"]].to_string())

print("=" * 100)
print("ICICI cases")
icici_rows = [
    # 3. auditlens: BIL/INFT/<numeric-ref>/<payee> (4 slash fields) -> payee name, not numeric ref
    row("BIL/INFT/003414169226/RAMESH KUMAR", "DEBIT", 4500.0),
    # 5. rk_ontheroad: leading direction word ahead of the name
    row("TRFR TO:JOHN DOE", "DEBIT", 3000.0),
    row("TRFR FROM:PRIYA SHARMA", "CREDIT", 3000.0),
    # regression guards
    row("BIL/INFT/003414169226/REMARKS/SURESH IYER", "DEBIT", 700.0),
    row("UPI/123456789012/Payment/swiggy@axis", "DEBIT", 300.0),
    row("MMT/IMPS/123456789012/Rent/ANIL/HDFC", "DEBIT", 15000.0),
]
out = run("ICICI", categorize_ICICI_transactions, icici_rows)
print(out[["description", "type", "transactionCategory", "transactionSubcategory", "partyName"]].to_string())

steps.message:
All five faults from the digest are found and fixed — each was a boundary/offset error inside an otherwise-correct rule, exactly as the maintainer predicted.

## Fixes

**1. All-numeric reference → cheque deposit lost** (`BankScripts/HDFC.py:100`)
The rule requires a 15-char remark but the regex `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` demands 11 zeros + 5 digits = 16 chars, so it could never fire; those credits fell through to the `TRANSFER` default. Changed to `^[0]{10}[0-9]{5}` (10 + 5 = 15).

**2. Bare-numeric salary narration → sub-tag lost** (`BankScripts/HDFC.py:124`)
The `^[0-9]{6}$` credit rule compared `accountType=="SAVINGS"`, but the service passes `"SAVING"` everywhere else (Controller, Purpose, ICICI, SBI, InternalPayment all use `"SAVING"`), so it never matched. Changed to `"SAVING"`.

**3. Leading direction word → empty/wrong counterparty** (`BankScripts/ICICI.py:159`)
`TRFR TO:<name>` / `TRFR FROM:<name>` extracted capture group `0` of `"TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)"` — the direction word itself — which downstream cleanup then blanked (`^[A-Z]{1,2}$`), leaving "From" or empty. Changed to group `1`, the name.

**4. Slash-delimited 4-field bill transfer → numeric ref as payee** (`BankScripts/ICICI.py:147`)
For `BIL/INFT/<numeric-ref>/<payee>` (exactly 3 slashes), the rule took slash field 2 — the numeric reference — instead of field 3, the final payee. Changed `sep_by_(...,2,3)` to `sep_by_(...,3,4)`, consistent with the 5-field variant on the next line which takes the last field.

**5. Offsetting credit right after matching debit → bounce instead of reversal** (`BankScripts/HDFC.py:98`)
The REVERSAL rule compared the description against `shift(periods=2)` while its type/amount conditions use `periods=1`, so adjacent debit/credit pairs skipped it and hit the generic `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` rule below. Changed to `periods=1` — matching the identical rule pair in ICICI.py:49-50.

## Verification
Ran each synthetic edge row through the full pipeline (categorizer → purpose → clean_names):
- 15-char remark `000000000012345` credit → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` (was `TRANSFER`)
- `123456` credit on SAVING → subcategory `SALARY` (was blank)
- `TRFR TO:JOHN DOE` / `TRFR FROM:PRIYA SHARMA` → `John Doe` / `Priya Sharma` (was empty / "From")
- `BIL/INFT/003414169226/RAMESH KUMAR` → `Ramesh Kumar` (was blanked numeric ref)
- Adjacent same-amount, same-description IMPS debit→credit → `REVERSAL` (was `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`)

Regression guards stayed byte-identical: ordinary UPI/NEFT/POS/salary-text rows, the 5-field `BIL/INFT/.../REMARKS/NAME` form, and a genuine non-transfer bounce pair still yields `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`.
